### **Job Description and Duties**

Have you been on the hunt for a position that spans Mono to Imperial Counties. Are you throwing out lines for opportunities that revolve around conservation and regulatory compliance? Are you electrified by the idea of working a blended office and field position within the wide territories of utility right of ways, which includes Lake Sabrina, Big Bear, the Mojave National Preserve, Owens Valley, and beyond?
  
  
The Inland Deserts Habitat Conservation Program is seeking a Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) to work throughout Region 6 as part of a Southern California team advancing compliance with Southern California Edison's (SCE) projects on public and private lands. This unit is designed to accelerate the pace and scale of utility environmental compliance, improving permitting pathways, and inspecting SCE's operations, maintenance, and capital projects when regulated by Fish and Game code. In this role, you will collaborate directly CDFW and SCE staff to permit projects that balance habitat form and function in both terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, supporting the recovery of declining species and enhancing ecological resilience, when California's public trust resources are affected by SCE's work under Fish and Game Code and CEQA. From desert springs, to vast lakes, to mountain meadows, your work will help conserve the Inland Deserts’ unique fish, wildlife, and native plants. We are looking for a motivated, independent, and innovative professional who thrives on problem-solving and partnership. If you’re ready to make a lasting impact on California’s wild landscapes and lead efforts that shape the future of the fish, wildlife, and plant resources of the state, apply now!

  

**Personal Leave Program:** Effective July 1, 2025, state employees are subject to temporary salary reductions ranging from 2% to 4.62% in exchange for Personal Leave Program (PLP) hours. Please note that the salary ranges listed in this Job Control may not reflect these reductions associated with the 2025 Personal Leave Program.

  

Please follow the link for more information regarding the 2025 Personal Leave program:

  

Personal Leave Program - Human Resources - CalHR.

This position may be eligible for a telework opportunity in accordance with departmental policies and operational needs. Beginning July 1, 2026, employees will be required to work in-person at least four (4) days per week in alignment with Executive Order N-22-25. Additional in-office days may be required based on operational needs.

**This position is a 12-month Limited Term (LT) and may be extended up to 24 months or become permanent.**

During this 12-month Limited Term assignment, you will receive full health, dental, and vision benefits! You will also earn State Service and accrue monthly leave credits.

  
  

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The position will be headquartered in the Ontario office, with site visits throughout the Inland Deserts Region, including Mono, Inyo, San Bernardino, Riverside, and Imperial Counties. Periodic travel up to 25% outside the Inland Deserts Region may also be required. The position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard and Microsoft Office software for up to eight hours per day, and to complete office tasks that involve sitting, standing, and walking to other locations. The role also includes coordinating and participating in meetings and conference calls, as well as attending in-person meetings and workgroups with stakeholders and local, state, and federal agencies within the Inland Deserts Region as well as Regions 4 and 5. Field site visits and travel will be necessary, and the incumbent must be able to walk on uneven, hilly terrain. The Position may require the incumbent to wear a uniform identifying the employee as CDFW staff. This position offers the possibility of an hybrid- telework agreement based on the Department's current Telework Policy.

### **Job Description and Duties**

**SENIOR ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (SPECIALIST) (PERMANENT INTERMITTENT) – COLORADO DESERT DISTRICT / DISTRICT WIDE / CUYAMACO RANCHO STATE PARK**

  

The reporting location for this position is Cuyamaca Rancho State Park in Julian, CA. This position will work under the general direction of Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory).

The Senior Environmental Scientist (Specialist) independently performs complex scientific, environmental planning, fire-management, project-development, and natural resource management assignments associated with wildfire-risk reduction and ecological resilience. The position develops and maintains District and park-unit fire management plans; develops prescribed-fire and fuel-treatment projects; prepares prescribed-burn plans and smoke-management documentation; coordinates environmental review, CEQA compliance, permits, operational readiness, implementation, monitoring, and reporting; and evaluates ecological and operational results following treatments. This position may lead projects, technical teams, field operations, training, contractors, and seasonal employees.

Training and Development Assignments may be considered.

Possession of a valid Class C driver’s license is required. You must answer the questions addressing your driver’s license on your application. Ensure you provide your driver’s license number, class, expiration date, and any endorsements and/or restrictions on your application.

The selected candidate is required to submit to a background investigation process utilizing Live Scan fingerprinting prior to appointment.

This position may work up to 1500 hours in any calendar year.

This position is designated as not telework eligible.

**State housing may be required.** For further information regarding this position, please contact Danny McCamish at (760) 522-2474 or at danny.mccamish@parks.ca.gov.

Special Requirement/Condition of Employment: Depending on the assigned location, the incumbent may be required to occupy state-owned housing to meet operational needs, or may be offered state-owned housing if available. Housing assignments will be determined in accordance with Department policy, operational priorities, and applicable labor agreements.

**This recruitment may be used to fill identical vacancies which may occur within 180 days of the Final Filing Date of this job posting.**

You will find additional information about the job in the **Duty Statement**.

### **Working Conditions**

The position requires a combination of professional office work and frequent field assignments throughout the Colorado Desert District. The incumbent will work across a wide range of environments, including low-elevation Colorado Desert ecosystems, desert riparian systems, chaparral, oak woodland, and montane conifer forest. Field assignments may involve rugged and remote terrain, steep slopes, unimproved roads, smoke, dust, ash, loud equipment, active vegetation-management operations, recently burned landscapes, and climatic conditions ranging from below freezing in the mountains to extreme desert heat. Work may require hiking substantial distances over uneven terrain and operation of four-wheel-drive State vehicles on paved and unpaved roads. Prescribed-fire, wildfire, emergency response, training, and project activities may require irregular work schedules, early mornings, evenings, weekends, overnight travel, and multi-day assignments. Daily office duties require use of computers, telephones, GIS and data-management applications, Microsoft Office applications, departmental databases, PFIRS, and other specialized scientific and project-management software.

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee receives a temporary reduction in pay in exchange for PLP 2025 leave credits. The percentage of the temporary salary reduction and the number of PLP 2025 leave credits are determined by the position’s assigned bargaining unit. **The salary range(s) included in this job advertisement do not reflect the temporary salary reduction.** For additional information regarding PLP 2025, please click here.

### **Job Description and Duties**

The Fish Restoration Program (FRP) is seeking two creative, curious, and collaborative scientists to help drive cutting edge ecological analysis, interagency coordination, and field based discovery related to tidal wetland restoration across the upper San Francisco Estuary. If you’re excited by the intersection of advanced analytics, restoration science, mentorship, and hands on fieldwork, this is your opportunity to make a direct impact on the future of California’s wetlands.

What You’ll Do

• Lead advanced ecological analyses to evaluate restoration effectiveness and guide adaptive management.

• Synthesize literature, data, and multi program findings into high quality technical reports and peer-reviewed articles.

• Mentor colleagues in data analysis, visualization, and effective scientific communication.

• Work closely with partner agencies to integrate monitoring and synthesis efforts and support responsible data access and use.

• Get outside—conduct boat-based sampling of wetland invertebrates and fishes in and around the eleven FRP restoration projects.

• Support lab operations by sorting invertebrate samples, preparing nutrient samples, and calibrating water quality instruments.

Who You Are

You’re a scientist who enjoys the entire process of transforming samples into knowledge – getting muddy, wrangling data, and communicating findings, while teaching others along the way. You thrive in collaborative, interdisciplinary environments and believe science should be transparent, rigorous, and accessible.

Why This Role Matters

FRP’s monitoring and synthesis will shape California’s wetland restoration planning and management for years to come. Your work will help determine what’s working, why it’s working, and how restoration can be improved to support fish and wildlife in a changing estuary.

Ready to put your analytical, ecological, and communication talents to work for one of the state’s most impactful restoration programs?

Apply today and help build a healthier estuary for future generations.

Field work involves kneeling, reaching, and lifting gear up to 40 pounds, may occur in inclement weather or rough water, and require early starts and long workdays. Must possess a valid driver's license and be prepared to operate a State vehicle.

jobs.description:
**Senior Environmental Scientist**

**Perth, WA | Permanent, Full-time / Part-time**

RPS, a Tetra Tech company, is a leading global professional services consultancy delivering solutions across the environment, infrastructure, energy and urban development sectors.

In Australia Asia Pacific, we work with industry, government and communities to define, design and manage complex projects that create shared value. Our people combine technical expertise with practical thinking to help clients understand environmental risks, navigate complex challenges and deliver successful project outcomes.

As part of Tetra Tech, we are connected to a global network of approximately 30,000 employees, providing access to specialist expertise, opportunities and projects across Australia and internationally.

**The Opportunity**

We are seeking a Senior Scientist to join our Oceans & Environment team in Perth, or Margaret River. RPS understand the importance of flexible working arrangements and this role is open to both full-time and part-time hours.

This is an excellent opportunity for an early to mid career environmental scientist who has experience in environmental approvals and is looking to continue developing their technical and consulting capability. Working alongside experienced environmental professionals, you will contribute to a range of projects.

**What you'll be involved in**

Your responsibilities will include:

* Preparing environmental approval documentation under the EP Act and EPBC Act.
* Preparing practical environmental management plans and strategies.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Manage multiple tasks on a range of projects and effectively deal with conflicting priorities and work to tight deadlines.
* Prepare and provide environmental advice to clients.
* Work as part of a multi-disciplinary team and work co-operatively with people at all levels to achieve outcomes.
* Communicate and maintain good relationships with internal stakeholders, clients, suppliers and project stakeholders.

**About you**

We are looking for someone who is technically curious, practical and keen to build a career in environmental approvals and environmental consulting.

**You will ideally bring:**

* A relevant tertiary qualification in environmental management or environmental science.
* Experience in undertaking environmental impact assessments in Western Australia.
* Understanding of State and Commonwealth environmental legislation, policy and guidance.
* Good technical report writing skills and attention to detail
* Minimum of five years relevant work experience.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills
* The ability to work independently while knowing when to seek technical guidance
* An understanding of project delivery including quality, safety, time and budget considerations
* A commitment to ongoing professional and technical development

**Why RPS?**

Joining RPS means becoming part of a collaborative environmental team while also having access to the technical capability and opportunities of the broader Tetra Tech network.

You will have the opportunity to develop your career alongside experienced contaminated land specialists, gain exposure to a diverse range of projects and progressively take on greater technical, project and client responsibilities.

**We also offer:**

* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where appropriate
* Professional development and career progression opportunities
* Paid professional memberships
* Active lifestyle and wellbeing initiatives
* Employee assistance and wellbeing support
* Opportunities to work with technical specialists across Australia and the wider Tetra Tech network
* A supportive and collaborative team environment
* Paid parental leave and other employee benefits

**Our commitment**

RPS is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where people are respected, supported and encouraged to bring their individual perspectives and experience to work.

If you have a foundation in environmental science or contaminated land and are looking for an opportunity to deepen your technical expertise while working alongside experienced specialists, we'd like to hear from you.

**Our Approach**

Our people live our purpose, deliver our promise, and demonstrate our behaviours every day. Our behaviours define who we are. Developed by our people, they underpin everything that we do. They create the memorable experiences we are known for and make RPS a great place to do great work.  
Stronger together is one of our five core behaviours and it is key to building a collaborative workplace. We encourage everyone to bring their best and to support others to do the same. By sharing knowledge, challenging each other to think differently, and fostering an environment of trust and respect, our people can learn, grow and thrive – and share in our success.

**Recruitment Agencies**

We have a Preferred Supplier List of trusted partners to assist us when required and do not acknowledge any speculative CVs or unsolicited candidate introductions from agencies not on this list. Please refer to the careers page on our website if you require any further information.

**Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist**
============================================================

**Senior Environmental Assessment and Approvals Specialist – Permanent and 12 month Secondment / Max Term Contract – Perth CBD**

  

We have two upcoming opportunities for Senior Assessment & Approvals Specialists to join our team on a Permanent and 12-month secondment / maximum term contract.

In this role, you will lead and support the development of strategic network plans and asset strategies. Your primary focus will be on clearly identifying SHE requirements associated with our work programs, influencing external stakeholders to secure strategic safety and environment statutory approvals and requirements for future growth, development and protection of the network.

**Bring your expertise. Build something meaningful in Bundaberg.**

Are you an experienced technical or project professional looking for an opportunity to combine meaningful project work with strong client relationships, business development and the potential to grow your leadership career?

We’re deliberately keeping our search broad. Your project management or technical background could be in transport, civil, water, structural, electrical, environment or another technical discipline. What matters most is your ability to bring strong consulting experience, work closely with clients and contribute to both project delivery and business growth.

**Build your career, and a great life, in Bundaberg**  
If you’ve been thinking about swapping the pace of a major city for a regional lifestyle without stepping back from your career, Bundaberg offers the opportunity to do both.

With the coast on your doorstep, a relaxed regional lifestyle and easy access to destinations such as Bargara and the Southern Great Barrier Reef, Bundaberg offers a different way to build your career. Whether you’re already based in Queensland or considering a move from interstate, it’s an opportunity to enjoy the benefits of regional living while continuing to develop your career with a global professional services company.

We’re particularly interested in people who enjoy combining hands-on project delivery with building trusted client relationships, identifying opportunities and growing the business.

You may already be an established senior professional, or you may be ready to broaden your influence, take on greater client and commercial responsibility and continue developing towards future leadership opportunities.

At GHD, you’ll have the opportunity to combine your technical expertise, project experience and client relationships while being connected to a broader multidisciplinary business. This isn’t about fitting into a narrowly defined role. We’re interested in what you could bring to Bundaberg.

GHD is an equal opportunity employer, and we want everyone to be able to fully participate in our recruitment process. We value a diverse workforce and an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples and people of all identities.

GHD embraces a range of flexible work practices to create a work environment focused on well-being, flexibility and productivity where our people can thrive.

We respectfully ask that no agency resumes be presented at this stage.
